title: CompTIA SecurityX (CAS-005)
summary: CompTIA SecurityX, exam code CAS-005, is the advanced, expert level security certification that replaced CompTIA Advanced Security Practitioner, or CASP+, in 2024. It targets senior security engineers, security architects and lead analysts who already hold a mid level certification and now design, integrate and govern security across an organisation. The exam tests judgement as much as knowledge, mixing multiple choice and performance based items in which you perform a task in a simulated environment. Passing it shows an employer that you can take a business requirement, choose controls, weigh risk and defend the decision to technical and non technical audiences. It supports roles such as security architect, senior security engineer and security consultant. The domain structure below follows the published objectives for CAS-005; confirm the current version with the vendor before booking. This is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with or endorsed by CompTIA.

beginner.definition: This is a high level security certification from CompTIA, an organisation that publishes vendor neutral information technology exams. The code is CAS-005 and the current name is SecurityX. It replaced an older exam called CompTIA Advanced Security Practitioner, or CASP+, and it is aimed at people with several years of security experience.
beginner.whyItMatters: Senior security jobs are not about knowing one tool; they are about making good decisions when money and time are limited. This certificate proves you can design a secure architecture, weigh risk and explain your choices to managers. It is often used to meet seniority requirements for government and defence contract work. For your career it signals readiness for architect or lead level responsibility rather than day to day administration.
howItWorks: Check that you meet the recommended experience first, because this exam assumes you have already worked in security for several years.
Study the five domains in order, and for each one link the theory to a real project you have worked on.
Practise performance based tasks, where you configure or analyse something on screen instead of choosing an answer.
Read architecture case studies and write short design notes, so you practise justifying a control choice.
Work through practice questions to find weak domains, then revisit the underlying concepts rather than memorising answers.
Book the exam when you can explain every domain to a colleague without notes.
beginner.example: Picture a hospital that wants doctors to reach patient records from home. A junior engineer asks which firewall to buy. A SecurityX level engineer asks different questions first. Who is allowed to see which records? What happens if a laptop is stolen? How do we prove later who opened a file? The certificate shows you can start with the business need and the risk, then choose technology that fits both, instead of reaching for a product name.
takeaways: This is an expert exam, so plan for significant study time on top of existing job experience.
Every domain rewards judgement about risk and trade-offs, not the recall of product features.
Confirm the current exam objectives and question format on the vendor website, since CASP+ was retired and replaced.

objectives: Translate a business requirement into a secure architecture with defined controls and clear trade-offs
Integrate security into engineering and development workflows without blocking delivery
Analyse risk data and choose treatments that match the organisation's stated risk appetite
Design identity, access and cryptographic solutions that scale across cloud and on premises systems
Evaluate security operations, monitoring and incident response capabilities and recommend improvements
Communicate security decisions and their cost to executives, auditors and technical teams

chapters.title: Security architecture
objectives: Apply established security architecture patterns and frameworks to a given business scenario
Compare on premises, cloud, hybrid and edge designs and justify the one that fits the requirement
Design resilient systems with redundancy, segmentation and failure handling built in
Embed security controls into system and software lifecycles from the first design conversation
Assess how emerging technology changes the threat picture and adjust the architecture accordingly

chapters.title: Security engineering
objectives: Select and configure cryptographic services, including key management and certificate handling
Design authentication, authorisation and identity federation for users, services and devices
Apply secure configuration and hardening baselines across servers, endpoints and network devices
Integrate security controls into continuous integration and delivery pipelines
Engineer secure communication channels and protect data in transit and at rest

chapters.title: Security operations
objectives: Design monitoring, logging and detection coverage that produces actionable alerts
Lead a response to a significant incident, including containment, evidence handling and recovery
Conduct and interpret vulnerability assessment and penetration test results
Plan continuity and disaster recovery arrangements and validate them through exercises
Automate repetitive operational and response tasks safely

chapters.title: Security governance, risk and compliance
objectives: Build and maintain a risk register and apply consistent treatment decisions
Map organisational controls to recognised frameworks, standards and regulatory obligations
Develop policies, standards and procedures that staff can actually follow
Prepare for and support audits, assessments and third party reviews
Advise leadership on security investment using quantified business language

chapters.title: Security program management
objectives: Align a security programme with business strategy, budget and measurable objectives
Manage third party and supply chain risk across the life of a contract
Build security awareness and training that changes behaviour rather than ticking a box
Track programme performance with meaningful metrics and report progress to stakeholders
Plan staffing, skills development and succession for the security function
